answer: Each row takes its turn at the irrigation channel, and the water keeper logs the day beside the row's name. A inlet turn claimed out of order fails the log: the channel must run exactly when the row's own day arrives, and a turn taken early leaves the next row dry. Stealing a season of water means bribing the keeper, forging a month of entries and paying 11,600, while the falcon page in the keeper's book is read at every watering, so a row whose turn was never written is shut off, and the pigment sluice is locked against any row out of turn.
